draw.sigma: sigma = sum over hops of the E/W tally times ln(qE/qW): (nE - nW)*ln(qE/qW) for constant arms
draw.init: x = w % n, y = (w >> log2 n) % n, counter step 0
draw.hop: counter step t = 1..T; direction = (w >> 24) against the cumulative thresholds [qE, qE+qW, qE+qW+qN, qE+qW+qN+qS]

corner.index: count sequence c = ∑_t c_t·5^t, c_t = walkers in the region at time t; times 0..k-1

claims.statement: checkerboard (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (h2 : 2 ∣ n) (t : ℕ) (c : ZMod 2) (s : State n) : labelMass n h2 t c ((stepState n)^[t] s) = labelMass n h2 0 c s
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.checkerboard
claims.doc:
Checkerboard (even n only): every particle carries the label
(x + y + t) mod 2 forever — streaming moves it to the other sublattice each
step and collisions happen within a sublattice — so the mass sitting on each
labelled checkerboard is conserved. The wrap across the periodic seam keeps
the labelling consistent only when n is even; odd n has no such invariant.

claims.statement: collide_collide (s : UInt32) : collide (collide s) = s
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.collide_collide
claims.doc: Collisions are their own inverse.

claims.statement: collide_flip : ∀ s : Fin 16, collide (flip s.val.toUInt32) = flip (collide s.val.toUInt32)
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.collide_flip
claims.doc: Collisions commute with velocity reversal.

claims.statement: collide_mass : ∀ s : Fin 16, mass (collide s.val.toUInt32) = mass s.val.toUInt32
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.collide_mass
claims.doc: Collisions conserve the particle number.

claims.statement: column_momentum_refuted : ∑ y, px16 (stepState 4 east4 (0, y)) ≠ ∑ y, px16 (east4 (0, y))
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.column_momentum_refuted
claims.doc:
Refuted: x-momentum is not conserved per column. A single east-going
particle on the 4×4 lattice carries its x-momentum from column 0 into
column 1 in one step. Per-row y-momentum fails the same way.

claims.statement: lightcone (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (t : ℕ) (p : Site n) (s₁ s₂ : State n) (h : ∀ q ∈ diamond n p t, s₁ q = s₂ q) : (stepState n)^[t] s₁ p = (stepState n)^[t] s₂ p
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.lightcone
claims.doc:
Light cone: after `t` steps the value at any site `p` depends only on
the initial values within lattice L1 distance `t` of `p` — the diamond
|dx| + |dy| ≤ t with periodic distance, so it wraps around the lattice.

claims.statement: lightcone_point (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (t : ℕ) (r p : Site n) (s₁ s₂ : State n) (h : ∀ q, q ≠ r → s₁ q = s₂ q) (hp : p ∉ diamond n r t) : (stepState n)^[t] s₁ p = (stepState n)^[t] s₂ p
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.lightcone_point
claims.doc:
A change at a single site `r` can only be seen, `t` steps later, at
sites within `r`'s diamond of radius `t`.

claims.statement: loschmidt_echo (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (t : ℕ) (s : State n) : revState n ((stepState n)^[t] (revState n ((stepState n)^[t] s))) = s
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.loschmidt_echo
claims.doc:
The Loschmidt echo: evolve `t` steps, reverse every velocity and collide,
evolve `t` steps, and do it again: every state returns to itself.

claims.statement: mass_conserved (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (s : State n) : ∑ p, mass16 (stepState n s p) = ∑ p, mass16 (s p)
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.mass_conserved
claims.doc: HPP conserves the total number of particles.

claims.statement: momentum_conserved (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (s : State n) : (∀ y : ZMod n, ∑ x, px16 (stepState n s (x, y)) = ∑ x, px16 (s (x, y))) ∧ (∀ x : ZMod n, ∑ y, py16 (stepState n s (x, y)) = ∑ y, py16 (s (x, y))) ∧ (∑ p, px16 (stepState n s p) = ∑ p, px16 (s p)) ∧ (∑ p, py16 (stepState n s p) = ∑ p, py16 (s p))
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.momentum_conserved
claims.doc:
HPP conserves momentum in the direction it can be carried: the
x-momentum of each row (#east − #west summed along the row) and the
y-momentum of each column are invariant, and so are both components of the
total momentum.

claims.statement: null_start (seed : UInt32) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : ∑ p, mass16 (nullState seed n p) = n * n / 8
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.null_start
claims.doc:
The null start of 001 is exact-`n²/8`: the uniform subset over all
`4n²` velocity slots holds exactly `n²/8` particles.

claims.statement: packed_start (seed : UInt32) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (h8 : 8 ∣ n) : ∑ p, mass16 (packedState seed n p) = n * n / 8 ∧ ∀ p : Site n, ¬ inRegion n (n / 2 - (n / 4) / 2) (n / 2 - (n / 4) / 2) (n / 4) p → packedState seed n p = 0
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.packed_start
claims.doc:
The packed start of 001: exactly `n²/8` particles — half the velocity
slots of the centred block of side `n/4` — and no particle outside the
block (the block geometry is exact once `8 ∣ n`, in particular for every
power-of-two lattice of the registered sizes).

claims.statement: step_inverse (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : Function.Bijective (stepState n) ∧ ∀ s : State n, stepState n (revState n (stepState n (revState n s))) = s ∧ revState n (stepState n (revState n (stepState n s))) = s
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.step_inverse
claims.doc:
One HPP step is a bijection. Its inverse is the step conjugated by
`revState`: reverse every velocity and collide (an involution), step, and do
both again. Plain velocity reversal does not invert the step — with
step = stream ∘ collide, flip ∘ step ∘ flip = stream⁻¹ ∘ collide, which
differs from step⁻¹ = collide ∘ stream⁻¹ because collisions and streaming
do not commute.

claims.statement: subset_mass (seed : UInt32) (n x0 y0 side count : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hx : x0 + side ≤ n) (hy : y0 + side ≤ n) : ∑ p, mass16 (subsetState seed n x0 y0 side count p) = min count (4 * side * side)
claims.name: TimesArrow.LatticeGas.subset_mass
claims.doc:
Selection sampling selects exactly the particles asked for: the
exact-`count` subset state of a lattice region holds exactly
`min count (4 · side²)` particles — every slot when the count exceeds the
region.

claims.statement: mirror_tilt_identity {α : Type*} [Fintype α] (p : PMF α) (κ : α → PMF α) (T : ℕ) (hac : ∀ ω, pathPMF p κ T (reversePath ω) = 0 → pathPMF p κ T ω = 0) : ∑ ω, (pathPMF p κ T ω).toReal * Real.exp (-2 * pathEntropyProduction p κ T ω) = ∑ ω, (pathPMF p κ T ω).toReal * Real.exp (pathEntropyProduction p κ T ω)
claims.name: TimesArrow.Markov.mirror_tilt_identity
claims.doc:
**The mirror tilt identity** (002, K4): the mean of `e ^ (-2σ)` under
the forward path law equals the mean of `e ^ σ`. With the integral
fluctuation theorem it gives the exact variance of the exponential-average
estimator, `(E [e ^ σ] - 1) / R`.

claims.statement: philox_kat : ∀ v ∈ kat, philox v.1 v.2.1 v.2.2.1 = v.2.2.2
claims.name: TimesArrow.Philox.philox_kat
claims.doc: Philox matches the Random123 known-answer vectors.

claims.statement: null_kernel_symmetric (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (i j : Site n) : walkerK n nullW nullW_sum i j = walkerK n nullW nullW_sum j i
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.null_kernel_symmetric
claims.doc: The registered null one-walker kernel is symmetric.

claims.statement: path_sigma_eq_hop_tally (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (h3 : 3 ≤ n) (M T : ℕ) (ω : Fin (T + 1) → Fin M → Site n) (hω : TimesArrow.Markov.pathPMF (uniformConfig n M) (prodK n M drivenW drivenW_sum) T ω ≠ 0) : TimesArrow.Markov.pathEntropyProduction (uniformConfig n M) (prodK n M drivenW drivenW_sum) T ω = (netHops n M T ω : ℝ) * Real.log 3
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.path_sigma_eq_hop_tally
claims.doc:
**Pathwise σ is the signed E/W hop tally** (M1, K1): on every
positive-probability trajectory of the driven product chain on a torus with
`3 ≤ n`, the path entropy production is the number of east hops minus the
number of west hops, times the drive `ln 3` — one integer per path, the
observable the simulation accumulates.

claims.statement: product_support_symmetric (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (M : ℕ) (w : Dir → ℕ) (hw : ∑ d, w d = 256) (hwpos : ∀ d, 0 < w d) (i j : Fin M → Site n) : prodK n M w hw i j = 0 ↔ prodK n M w hw j i = 0
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.product_support_symmetric
claims.doc:
Support symmetry of the product chain: with positive weights every joint
move has its reverse available (M1).

claims.statement: product_uniform_stationary (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (M : ℕ) (w : Dir → ℕ) (hw : ∑ d, w d = 256) : TimesArrow.Markov.IsStationary (prodK n M w hw) (uniformConfig n M)
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.product_uniform_stationary
claims.doc:
The `M`-walker product chain preserves the uniform configuration law for
every normalized weight vector: the registered uniform constructor is
exactly stationary for every arm (M1).

claims.statement: reversed_arm_is_reversal (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (M T : ℕ) : TimesArrow.Markov.reversedPathPMF (uniformConfig n M) (prodK n M drivenW drivenW_sum) T = TimesArrow.Markov.pathPMF (uniformConfig n M) (prodK n M reversedW reversedW_sum) T
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.reversed_arm_is_reversal
claims.doc:
**The reversed arm is the time reversal** (K3): with the uniform start,
the path law of the E↔W-swapped weights is exactly the law of the
time-reversed trajectories of the driven chain.

claims.statement: support_symmetric (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (w : Dir → ℕ) (hw : ∑ d, w d = 256) (hwpos : ∀ d, 0 < w d) (i j : Site n) : walkerK n w hw i j = 0 ↔ walkerK n w hw j i = 0
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.support_symmetric
claims.doc:
Positive direction weights give unconditional support symmetry for the
one-walker kernel: every allowed hop has its reverse available.

claims.statement: uniform_stationary (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (w : Dir → ℕ) (hw : ∑ d, w d = 256) : TimesArrow.Markov.IsStationary (walkerK n w hw) (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Site n))
claims.name: TimesArrow.Walker.uniform_stationary
claims.doc:
Every normalized walker weight vector preserves the uniform one-walker
distribution on a nonempty torus (the kernel is doubly stochastic).
